LESSON: CERAMICS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for production.
Topic 3.2: Ceramics
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 7

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Ceramics, part of Materials for production. in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are ceramic materials identified? 2. Why are ceramic materials important to society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Ceramics together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: A learner acquires evaluation and decision making skills when collecting items made of ceramic

materials in the locality.

18

• Citizenship: A learner demonstrates social cultural sensitivity and awareness when visiting workplaces in the locality to explore the uses of

ceramic materials.

Values:
• Responsibility: A learner engages in assigned roles and duties when collecting items made of ceramic materials in the locality,

• Unity: A learner collaborates with others when using a chart to match ceramic materials with their use in the work environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: A learner identifies potential dangerous materials when investigating the physical properties of ceramic materials.

• Learner protection: A learner takes care of himself or herself while collecting items made of ceramic materials in the locality.

Link to other Learning area:

A learner is able to relate the skills learnt when identifying items made of ceramic materials to pottery in Creative Arts.

Suggested learning resources:

• Realia [pottery, ceramic utensils, glasses, shells].

• Immediate or local environment.

• Digital devices with assistive technology.
